name: Mean-reversion fade of upside over-extension (range-gated short)
rationale: The reversion-after-extension edge from the SHORT side: when bb_z is statistically stretched far above the band (an over-extended, exhausted up-move), price tends to snap back toward the mean at the swing horizon. We take the downside snap-back as a short (direction -1: stop sits ABOVE entry, take-profit BELOW). This is the deliberate MIRROR of the oversold-dip long that already exists in the family, so it is genuinely distinct, not a re-skin. A low-ADX gate (adx lt adx_ceiling) is the key guard: we only fade an extension in a CHOPPY/range regime where mean-reversion pays, and stand aside when ADX is high and the same high bb_z is a trend breakout that keeps running. The Bollinger window (bb_lb) is fitted, not magic, so the z-score is consistent with the regime. HONEST PRIOR: spot-only fade-the-rip on daily bars has shown no robust edge after costs and shorting spot is not even executable on Binance spot, so a powered FAIL is the expected, useful outcome; the value is a clean, leak-free test of the short-extension leg of the family.
catalyst: upside over-extension exhausts in a non-trending regime and mean-reverts down
